title: He screamed when the iron disappeared.
paragraphs: He screamed when the iron disappeared.

And suddenly the river swallowed more than metal.
It swallowed dignity.
Responsibility.
Reputation.
The next moment he was panicking.
This is the tension of 2 Kings 6:5–7.

“Alas, master! for it was borrowed.”
— 2 Kings 6:5
Feel the weight of that sentence.

This wasn’t a careless man swinging lazily in the forest.
This was a man doing the work of God with the sons of the prophets.

One swing too hard.
The iron axe head flies off the handle.
And the man collapses into a desperate cry:
That line is deeper than we think.
Because sometimes the pain of loss isn’t just about the object.
It’s about the responsibility attached to it.
Some of you know this feeling.

A calling.
A marriage.
A ministry.
A reputation.
A spiritual fire.
And the enemy whispers the same accusation:
But watch what the prophet Elisha does.
He doesn’t say, “You should have been more careful.”
Instead, he asks one simple question:
That question is dripping with mercy.
God does not begin restoration with condemnation.
Where did the prayer life begin to fade?
Where did the secret compromise start?
Where did the passion for Christ grow cold?
Where did the edge of your spiritual axe become dull?
God asks the question not because He doesn’t know.
He asks because healing starts with honesty.
You cannot recover what you refuse to locate.
So the man points to the water.
Something that breaks every law of nature.
“He cut a stick and threw it there.”
The thing that should sink by nature rises by the power of God.
But hidden inside the miracle is something even deeper.
Because notice what triggered the miracle.
A piece of wood entered the place where the iron had sunk.
Because centuries later another piece of wood would touch the place where humanity sank.
Humanity fell into the deep waters of sin.
But then Christ stepped into our drowning place.
The wood of the cross entered the waters of our judgment.
And through His death and resurrection…
Because the Gospel is the greatest floating-axe-head miracle ever told.
What was impossible for man became possible through Christ.
What sank in your life is not sovereign.
That calling you think you lost.
God specializes in raising what should stay sunk.
The story doesn’t end with the miracle though.
Elisha tells the man something powerful:
But you must pick it up.
Some people pray for miracles they refuse to grab.
Some ask for restoration but will not step forward to receive it.
But the moment that man reached down and grabbed the floating iron—
If this message speaks to you today, pause for a moment and ask yourself honestly:
Because the God who made iron float…
Can raise anything that sank in your life.
And that is the scandal of grace.
The cross still reaches into deep waters.
The Savior still lifts the drowning.
Because someone on your timeline is standing by the river today…
But God is still asking the same question.
And the miracle may be closer than they think.
